attributes.size: plates ~55 μm length, 11 μm width; colonies ~48 μm
attributes.morphology: lamellar plates and massive grain boundary network

evidence.quote: The microstructure of as-sintered Ti64 alloy consists of large colonies of lamellar α plates and massive grain boundary α (GB-α) network, shown in Fig. 1 (a). The dimensions of the α plates are around 55 μm in length and 11 μm in width, while the size of the α colonies is approximately 48 μm, as determined by Image-Pro.

attributes.morphology: Widmanstätter structure with long and straight α lath

evidence.quote: After 60 % deformation, a Widmanstätter structure with long and straight α lath appears in the matrix.

attributes.size: length-width ratio of α lath decreases significantly

evidence.quote: After 80 % deformation, the length-width ratio of α lath in the lamellar structure decreases significantly, showing a typical basket-weave microstructure.

attributes.size: 10–50 μm in length and 2–3 μm in width

evidence.quote: After 950 ℃ /30 min annealing (Fig. 3 (a, b)), the microstructure consists of mainly interconnected platelike α with 10–50 μm in length and 2–3 μm in width,
a small volume fraction of block-shaped β transformed structure (β t) and thin β strips between α lath.

After solution and aging (Fig. 3 (e, f)), the RD-ND plane of the plate possesses a bimodal structure that consisted of equiaxed or long strip primary α (α p) with a grain size of about 10–20 μm and transformed β with fine acicular secondary α (α s).
transformed β with fine acicular secondary α (α s).
a network of secondary β phase can be seen in the enlarged α p area, seen in Fig. 3 (f).

From RD-TD plane in Fig. 2 (a1-d1), the intact original β grain can be observed in the sample of 60 % deformation. With increase of deformation, the original β grain virtually vanished, leaving only a little quantity of broken discontinuous grain boundary α. The average size of the original β grain after hot rolling is 200–400 μm.

In comparison to sintered materials, the tensile strength and yield strength are enhanced by 212 MPa after hot rolling, while the ductility is notably improved by 5.7 %.

suggesting that the change of grain morphology during β rolling is mainly controlled by dynamic recovery mechanism, followed by dynamic recrystallization.
